To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aconitine is converted into a potent and highly selective α7 nicotinic ligands by the introduction of an ester‐linked benzoyl side chain.

(1) The ester‐linked side chain of MLA is necessary for its nicotinic activity, (2) The norditerpenoid scaffold is necessary for α7‐nicotinic activity, and (3) The combination of the norditerpenoidal scaffold and the ester‐linker side chain confers α7‐nicotine receptor selectivity.

the ester linkage of the 2‐(methyssuccinimido)‐benzoyl‐group is required for the nicotinic receptor‐binding activity of methyllycaconitines, but the α7‐selectivity of these compounds is due to the norditerpenoidal structure of the molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new series of potent α7‐nicotinic ligands with the potential to be developed as therapeutic agents.
the development of novel ligands for the nicotinic acetycholine receptor and the elucidation of the structural requirements for subtype selectivity and potency.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2‐(succinimido)-benzoyl substituent is necessary for binding to the nicotinic site, but the norditerpenoids are the pharmacophores for α7 selectivity.

the norditerpenol moiety of MLA is the structural determinant of α7‐selectivity and the 2‐(succinimido)methylbenzoyl ester moiety is the determinant of nicotinic activity, and that the combination of both groups is necessary for high affinity binding.
aconitine and its congeners are not nicotinic ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MLA is a norditerpenoidal ester, and that its α7 selectivity derives from the norditerpenoidal core, while nicotinic potency derives from the ester‐linking moiety.
aconitine can be converted into MLA by the addition of a single chemical group.
aconitine and its congeners are potent activators of voltage‐gated sodium channels, but are not potent nicotinic ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aconitine is a useful scaffold from which potent and selective nicotinic ligands may be derived, and that the 2‐(succinimido)methylbenzoyl ester is a useful chemical motif for nicotinic ligandedrugs.
the 2‐(succinimido)methylbenzoyl ester group is necessary to confer nicotinic activity to norditerpenoids, and the norditerpenoids are the structural basis for subtype selectivity.
nicotinic activity is not a general property of norditerpenoid ligands, but rather is a property of the MLA scaffold.
